incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: cache-prefetch-service reporting prefix miss spike > 4x baseline for the last 12m. Impacting /v1/generate hosted tier. Pager: maria (oncall).

maria (oncall): On it. Can someone pull customer impact and a quick hit-rate trend?

dan (support): Seeing an uptick in 502s from some customers with high-concurrency streams. Example ticket: #C-2091 — intermittent failures between 12:04 and 12:18 UTC. Affected customers: acme-inc (prod), docs-ai (staging).

sanjay: I'm looking at prefix_kv_hitrate: we have a sharp drop starting 12:02 UTC. Local query: `sum(rate(prefix_kv_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(prefix_kv_lookups[5m]))` shows hitrate from ~0.92 -> 0.45.

kai: grabbing logs from the warmers and cachectl. Logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/q/90kX (shared). Relevant error: `WARN cache: failed to apply invalidation batch: context deadline exceeded` repeated 12:01-12:03.

maria (oncall): Timeline so far: incident-bot page at 12:05. Hitdrop starts ~12:02. First 502s observed ~12:04. Useful to track: any rollout or config change at 11:55-12:05?

ash: I see a deploy pipeline step for prefix-cache v2 rolled out to 30% at 11:58 (rollout id: rl-1287) that included an invalidation change.

priya: That rollout was intended to improve eviction policy (LRU->segmented-LRU) and added batched invalidations for stale prefixes. Could be related.

sanjay: Hypothesis A: batched invalidations raced with warmup leading to wide prefix missstorm. Hypothesis B: rewarm workers throttled (deadline errors) -> zeroing of prefix entries. Hypothesis C: key entropy change from the rollout caused poor reuse.

kai: Adding raw metrics snippet for the thread (prometheus queries):
```
# prefix lookups and hits
prefix_lookups_total{env="prod"} 1.2e6
prefix_hits_total{env="prod"} 1.1e6 -> 5.6e5 (after 12:02)
# rewarm worker errors
count_over_time(cache_rewarm_errors[10m]) = 83
```

maria (oncall): Live mitigation executed: 12:12 - paused rollout rl-1287 (30% -> 0%), 12:15 - scaled rewarm workers +2 (from 6 -> 8), 12:20 - increased prefix cache soft limit by 15%. Traffic shift to fallback pool at 12:22 for noisy tenants (docs-ai).

dan (support): After mitigation, customer 502s dropped ~70% by 12:28. Docs: https://support.redwood.internal/tickets/C-2091 (private).

ash: I pulled the invalidation job logs — looks like the invalidation batching code opened a single request for ~1200 keys, which timed out at the KV service when network jitter hit. That caused incomplete invalidation acknowledgements and a subsequent conservative rewarm that zeroed prefixes.

kai: Relevant stack trace snippet from warmers: `panic: rewarm timeout; falling back to cold fill` — we should paste that in RCA.

sanjay: Quick check: was there any TTL change? I don't see TTL updates in config history between 11:40-12:10. So TTL-sync gap less likely.

priya: Customer impact summary (from support and metrics): - ~5% of hosted API requests saw elevated latency/502s for 24 customers (15 small, 9 medium) between 12:04-12:30. Major customers had <1% error rate increase because of fallback pools.

maria (oncall): Actions taken (in-thread): 1) paused rollout rl-1287 2) reverted batching size config in invalidator to 200 keys (from 1200) 3) scaled rewarm workers 4) increased cache soft limit 5) routed noisy tenants to fallback pool. All mitigations completed by 12:30.

ash: Temporary config we applied (as a note to ops): `invalidator.batch_size=200` `invalidator.timeout=3s` `rewarm.concurrency=8`

kai: For the RCA we need: timeline (we have), invalidation logs (shared link above), rewarm worker stacks, and a reproducer for the batching timeout. I'm creating a repro job that simulates 1.2k invalidations under KV latency.

sanjay: Early root cause hypothesis: the invalidation batching change (rollout rl-1287) increased single-batch size which, under brief KV latency, caused timeouts. The timeout path didn't mark invalidations as partial properly and triggered rewarmer conservative behavior (cold fill) causing hit-rate collapse.

maria (oncall): Short-term follow-ups: - sanjay + kai to assemble repro and mitigation test - ash to write rollback postmortem draft - priya to prepare customer-facing summary for affected tenants - dan to follow up on all affected tickets. Owner assignments: sanjay (reproducer), ash (postmortem), priya (customer comms).

priya: I'll draft a one-paragraph note for customers: "We observed a temporary cache invalidation-induced missstorm tied to a recent rollout. We've paused the rollout and mitigations are in place. We're investigating and will follow up with technical postmortem"

dan (support): I'll queue templates for impacted customers and flag high-touch accounts for SE outreach.

maria (oncall): Closing the live mitigation stage. Setting severity->post-incident RCA. If anything re-escalates ping me directly. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated -> RCA_review_required.

kai: Note — add metric to alert on invalidation batching failures (count_over_time(cache_invalidator_failures[5m]) > 5) and a warmup fallback ratio alert.

sanjay: Will open the RCA doc and link it here. Draft: https://docs.redwood.internal/rca/2351234567-invalidation-batch-hitrate.json

ash: Quick logs export for the postmortem attached: https://logs.redwood.internal/export/2351234567.zip (retention: 14d).

maria (oncall): Thanks all. We'll reconvene tomorrow 10:00 UTC for blameless RCA. Action items: sanjay (repro + patch), ash (postmortem draft), priya (customer comms), kai (alerts), dan (tickets).

priya: adding customers list to the RCA doc now.

sanjay: small note — patch will add idempotency checks to invalidator and handle partial ack states explicitly.

maria (oncall): End of thread — marking root as 2351234567.
